patterns.title: Intune did not detect the app after install
patterns.summary: The installer ran but the Intune detection rule did not find the app afterwards, so Intune reports the install as failed.

remediation.action: Compare the rule with what the installer really wrote
remediation.detail: Check the exact MSI product code, file version or registry value on a device that has the app installed.
Registry and file rules default to the 64-bit view for 64-bit apps; for 32-bit installers use the right view or enable 'Run script as 32-bit'.
A custom detection script must write something to STDOUT and exit 0 to count as detected.
Use 'greater than or equal to', not 'equals', so updates still pass.

patterns.title: Content download failed
patterns.summary: The device could not download the app content.

remediation.detail: Confirm the device can reach the Intune content endpoints through any proxy or firewall.
A bad DO group or peer setting can stall content. Test with DO set to HTTP only.
Content is staged locally before install.

patterns.title: Downloaded content failed integrity check
patterns.summary: The downloaded content does not match its expected hash. It was corrupted in transit or altered by something in the path.

remediation.detail: Clear the IME content cache on one test device and re-sync.
SSL inspection or a caching proxy can alter content; bypass it for Intune content hosts.
If it keeps failing, rebuild the .intunewin and upload it again.

patterns.title: Install or operation timed out
patterns.summary: Something ran past its allowed time. Intune stops Win32 installs that run longer than the configured limit (60 minutes by default).

remediation.detail: Check the timestamps to see where the time went (download, install, waiting on a prompt).

remediation.action: Make sure the install is silent
remediation.detail: A hidden dialog waiting for input will time out every time.

remediation.action: Raise the maximum run time if justified
remediation.detail: Set it on the app, but only after confirming the install is genuinely slow.

patterns.title: A script or app used an Entra application that does not exist in this tenant
patterns.summary: A request to Microsoft Entra ID was rejected because application (client) ID {detail} is not registered in this tenant (AADSTS700016). When this appears in Intune script output, it is the script's own sign-in that failed, not the device's.

remediation.action: Find which script is making the call
remediation.detail: Look at the policy ID near the error in the Intune logs, then find that script in Intune (Devices, Scripts and remediations, or Platform scripts). Search it for the client ID.

remediation.action: Fix the application ID or tenant in the script
remediation.detail: Scripts copied from another tenant often keep the old client ID and tenant ID. Use the app registration from your own tenant.

remediation.action: Check the app registration exists and has consent
remediation.detail: If the app should exist, confirm it was not deleted and that an admin has consented to it.

verification: The script's error output no longer contains AADSTS700016.
The script reports its data or result successfully.

patterns.title: A script or app used an invalid or expired client secret
patterns.summary: Microsoft Entra ID rejected a client secret: it is wrong (AADSTS7000215) or has expired (AADSTS7000222).

remediation.action: Create a new client secret and update the script or app
remediation.detail: Secrets expire, usually after 6 to 24 months. Store the new one where the script reads it from.

remediation.action: Find the owner of the app registration
remediation.detail: Check Entra ID, App registrations, Certificates and secrets for the expiry date.

patterns.title: Authentication or token failure
patterns.summary: A request to Entra ID or the Intune service was rejected for an authentication reason. Check whether the message comes from Intune itself or from the output of a script it ran.

remediation.action: Work out who was signing in
remediation.detail: Intune's own sign-in problems point at the device (registration, clock, network). A message inside a script's error output points at that script.

remediation.action: Check device registration if it is Intune itself
remediation.detail: Confirm the device is Entra joined or hybrid joined and the PRT is healthy.
The code in the log identifies the exact rejection reason.

patterns.title: A remediation or detection script wrote an error but exited normally
regex: Detect error even if exit code is \d+, error = (?P<detail>[^\r\n]{0,160})
patterns.summary: Intune logged an error from a health script even though the script exited with its normal code: {detail}

remediation.detail: Add -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue (or try/catch) where a missing item is expected, so the error stream stays clean.
A script that reads HKCU: or user folders needs 'Run this script using the logged-on credentials' set, otherwise it looks in the wrong profile.

patterns.title: App requirement rule not met
patterns.summary: The device did not meet the app's requirement rules, so Intune skipped the install as 'not applicable'.

remediation.detail: Check OS version, architecture, disk space and any custom requirement script against the device.

patterns.title: App dependency failed
patterns.summary: A dependency app did not install or was not detected, so the parent app did not run.

remediation.detail: Open the dependency's own log entries and resolve that failure; the parent will follow.

patterns.title: Install needs a signed-in user but none is available
patterns.summary: The app is set to install in user context (or needs a user session) and nobody was signed in.

remediation.detail: Set install behaviour to System unless the app genuinely needs the user profile.

remediation.action: Otherwise schedule for when users are signed in
